_comment: Every app-visible change serial 4 makes against serial 3 (scripts/validate.py --declared ci/serial4-declared.json --baseline ci/serial3-baseline.json --previous-ref <serial 3>). Serial 3's own list stays in ci/serial3-declared.json (meshTerm's tests read a byte-identical copy of that one).

changes.reason: The AppArmor branch loads its profile with apparmor_parser -r (no systemd needed; serial 3 restarted apparmor.service, which fails without systemd) and runs only where apparmor_parser exists (no AppArmor userspace: nothing to load into, and a container on a restricting host has no /etc/apparmor.d: the serial-3 GitHub runner failure). A profile file of ours that exists but is not loaded (/sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles) is loaded (review 2026-10-12).
Kali keeps the Debian family's apt text: the same apparmor_parser change. A profile file of ours that exists but is not loaded (/sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles) is loaded (review 2026-10-12).

Arch: pacman -S --needed first, -Syu only when that fails (a stale or missing sync database), so a one-tap fix rarely upgrades the whole system (review 2026-10-12). (serial 3's -S alone failed 'target not found' on a fresh Arch with no sync database)

The unknown-family chain gains zypper and pacman (Containers sends Arch and openSUSE as unknown) and fails with a message where no package manager it knows is found (serial 3 exited 0 having installed nothing). pacman -S --needed first, -Syu only when that fails (a stale or missing sync database), so a one-tap fix rarely upgrades the whole system (review 2026-10-12). zypper's informational exits (100-103, 106 repository refresh failed, 107 scriptlet failed) count as installed; 104 (not found) and the rest fail (review 2026-10-12).

The unknown-family chain gains zypper (ca-certificates with ca-certificates-mozilla, the bundle) and pacman, and fails with a message where no package manager it knows is found. pacman -S --needed first, -Syu only when that fails (a stale or missing sync database), so a one-tap fix rarely upgrades the whole system (review 2026-10-12). zypper's informational exits (100-103, 106 repository refresh failed, 107 scriptlet failed) count as installed; 104 (not found) and the rest fail (review 2026-10-12).

Arch: get.docker.com refuses it ('Unsupported distribution'); Arch's docker package; ONE admin step (owner requirement: rootful Docker in one tap): install, the docker group (groupadd -f -r), reset-failed and enable --now where systemd runs, and the user's join unless the user is root (Containers offers these hosts install-script and join-group as separate rows, so the install line carries the join itself). A no-sudo host's su -c keeps the user's PATH, so the line adds them before groupadd/usermod (review 2026-10-12). pacman -S --needed first, -Syu only when that fails (a stale or missing sync database), so a one-tap fix rarely upgrades the whole system (review 2026-10-12). A full upgrade that replaced the running kernel (its /usr/lib/modules directory gone) stops with 'reboot the server, then tap Check Again' before starting Docker.

A full upgrade that replaced the running kernel (its /usr/lib/modules directory gone) stops with 'reboot the server, then tap Check Again' before starting Docker.

openSUSE: get.docker.com refuses it; openSUSE's docker package; ONE admin step (owner requirement: rootful Docker in one tap): install, the docker group (groupadd -f -r), reset-failed and enable --now where systemd runs, and the user's join unless the user is root (Containers offers these hosts install-script and join-group as separate rows, so the install line carries the join itself). A no-sudo host's su -c keeps the user's PATH, so the line adds them before groupadd/usermod (review 2026-10-12). zypper's informational exits (100-103, 106 repository refresh failed, 107 scriptlet failed) count as installed; 104 (not found) and the rest fail (review 2026-10-12).

Device finding 2026-10-12 (a Debian host whose docker group was deleted): usermod refused the join ('group docker does not exist', rc 6); the line creates the group first (groupadd -f -r: a no-op where it exists). The rootful one-step install-complete row &&-combines this line, so it gains the same. A no-sudo host's su -c keeps the user's PATH (on Debian no /usr/sbin or /sbin), so the line adds them before groupadd/usermod (review 2026-10-12).

Device finding 2026-10-12 (a Debian host whose docker group was deleted): docker.socket (SocketGroup=docker) failed, so 'systemctl enable --now docker' failed its dependency job; the line creates the group, clears the failed units (reset-failed), then enables and starts. A no-sudo host's su -c keeps the user's PATH (on Debian no /usr/sbin or /sbin), so the line adds them before groupadd/usermod (review 2026-10-12). The group step comes first and stops the line (one refusal for a non-sudoer); reset-failed runs only when systemctl is-failed says so, and never fails the line.

The same group and reset-failed steps before 'systemctl start docker'. A no-sudo host's su -c keeps the user's PATH (on Debian no /usr/sbin or /sbin), so the line adds them before groupadd/usermod (review 2026-10-12). The group step comes first and stops the line (one refusal for a non-sudoer); reset-failed runs only when systemctl is-failed says so, and never fails the line.

The same group and reset-failed steps before 'systemctl start docker.socket'. A no-sudo host's su -c keeps the user's PATH (on Debian no /usr/sbin or /sbin), so the line adds them before groupadd/usermod (review 2026-10-12). The group step comes first and stops the line (one refusal for a non-sudoer); reset-failed runs only when systemctl is-failed says so, and never fails the line.
Alpine: the docker group is created when missing, before the daemon starts (its socket's group) and before the user joins it

A no-sudo host's su -c keeps the user's PATH, so the line adds them before groupadd/usermod (review 2026-10-12).

apparmor_parser -r loads the profile (serial 3 restarted apparmor.service, which needs systemd); a message and a non-zero exit where apparmor_parser is missing; a profile file of ours that exists but is not loaded is loaded; /usr/sbin and /sbin added to PATH (review 2026-10-12).
